utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [B/C/S translation on channel 4]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [B/C/S translation on channel 4]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see on the transcript, this is just unacceptable. I mean it's -- could you please put on the record that the Registrar did -- her microphone was switched on. And I see that there is no record of her calling the case. Neither have I. I don't even have a translation. Can you hear the interpretation? No, I can't hear any interpretation and I'm on channel 4. I'm still not okay. It's plugged in. I can't hear a thing. Let's see with another set of ear phones. I can't hear a thing. At least I mean they are hearing me complaining that I am not hearing anything. They should speak and say something. At least and if everyone else is hearing, why shouldn't I hear as well?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour can you hear the English booth?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear some English words being spoken at last, yes. And now can I ask why there is no record of the Registrar calling the case, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just was informed by the translation booth that there was a mix-up with the channel so that should be the reason that there was no record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Could you call the case, again, Madam Registrar, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Brdjanin, can you here me in a language that you can understand? I hope you can hear.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour, yes, I hear and I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Brdjanin and good morning to you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Good morning, Anna Richterova for the Prosecution assisted by Hasan Younis case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you madam and good morning to you both. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours I'm John Ackerman and I'm here with Mr. Brian Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to you both. So I understand that there are some minor points that you would like to raise before we bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Exactly. There is really a minor point. I discussed the protective measures with the witness 7.266, we requested closed session. I discussed this issue with the witness and she agrees to open session if she is -- if she was granted facial distortion and pseudonym. She is not concerned of people where she lives but in connection with her work, she travelled all over the places and she would appreciate if her -- she wasn't recognised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I have no objection to that at all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So we were about to hand down our decision in any case so we just handed it down. I don't know what -- this witness will testify with protective measures that she -- that you have indicated, Madam Richterova, that is facial distortion and --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And pseudonym. If at any time obviously if you require to go into private session, then we would go into private session as and if necessary but no closed session as far as we are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The second thing was we requested closed session for the Witness 7.157.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is that BT89?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It is BT89.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: BT89 is going to be closed session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It is a female witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Our decision is as follows. It will be handed down in writing but basically this is what we are deciding, that both as regards BT88 and as regards BT89, they will be referred to by these respective pseudonyms at all times in the course of the testimony, or whenever referred to in the course of the proceedings, whether during the hearing or in documents, including the transcript of the proceedings. The testimony of Witness BT89, which is the one after the next, shall be held in closed session. All hearings to consider the issue of protective measures of the Witness BT89 shall be held in closed session, and edited record and transcripts of the said sessions shall be released to the public after review by the Prosecution in consultation with the VWS. The name addresses and whereabouts of BT89 shall be sealed and not included in any of the public records of the Tribunal. And the usual other details of such decisions, including that the testimony of BT89 shall be sealed and shall not be released to the public or media in any form. So in the meantime we can proceed with BT88. It's BT88, yes you have to draw down until she comes in and then --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I have one small issue. I already discussed it with Mr. Ackerman. We would like to swap the Witness 7.156 with the Witness 7.157 so it means that after Witness 7.266, which will testify in open session today, tomorrow we would call the Witness 7.157.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. If you have no problems with that, Mr. Ackerman, we can proceed that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour I have no problems as long as we don't start with 7.157 today since I only learned about this this morning, although Ms. Richterova made efforts to reach me by e-mail and fax yesterday my system was broken down and not working and she wasn't able to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mine too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Unfortunately I didn't learn about it until this morning so I didn't have any materials here at all so we could start that witness in the morning. I hunch we will finish maybe a few minutes early today then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. I have no idea. I don't know how long you anticipate your in chief to last.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I expect two hours but Your Honours know that you can expect one and the reality is different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I meant to say actually or the reason why I mention this is that I feel -- I don't know whether you would agree with me, but I feel Mr. Ackerman's complaint is fully justified if he was not prepared to start with the evidence of 7.157 today he should not be put in that position.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Of course we just discussed it and he agreed with tomorrow and I already informed VW about this. Just for the record, Ann Sutherland joined the Prosecution team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, madam. I take it you can follow what I'm saying in a language that you can understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So good morning once more. You are about to give evidence. I will explain to you later on under which conditions, in the meantime, before you start your evidence, it is required by our rules that you enter a solemn declaration equivalent to an oath, that you will be telling us the truth, and the whole truth in the course of your testimony. The text of the solemn declaration is contained in a piece of paper which Madam usher is going to hand to you now. Please read that solemn declaration aloud and that will be your undertaking with this Tribunal that you will be speaking the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. I take it that this is the first time that you are giving evidence before this Tribunal, and therefore I will explain to you very briefly what's going to happen. You are first going to be asked a set of questions by the Prosecution, today being led by Madam Richterova. I suppose that you know her already. You have met her already. She will then be followed by Mr. Ackerman -- have you been following, have you been hearing what I was saying or did you have difficulties? She will then, Madam Richterova, she will then be followed by Mr. John Ackerman, who is the lead counsel for Radoslav Brdjanin who is the accused in this case. He will be cross-examining you. Now, you asked for and we have granted you some what we call some protective measures, and basically they are two. The first one is that no one will refer to you by your name here but we will be referring to you by a pseudonym, by a nom de plume. You are just being -- going to be referred to by a number, and a couple of letters. You are BT88. BT88. And that's how you will go into the records of this case, and any documents that are handed down and out to the public will not bear your name but your pseudonym only. That's number 1. Number 2 is that although others will be able to hear and follow your testimony, no one will be able to see your face, and that's because we have granted you visual, facial distortion, image distortion. In other words if you look at your monitor right in front of you, if it is on video mode, and that's what others will see you like. That's how you appear to others. In other words, your image is completely distorted and no one should be able to see your face anywhere outside this court. Having explained that, I will now invite Madam Richterova to start with her examination-in-chief. One bit of advice. Please answer the question, the whole question, and nothing but the question. Don't go round in circles, don't give us long stories. We are only interested in the answer that is specific to the question or questions that are put to you in sequence. So try to answer those questions. Otherwise you will be here for days and no one will enjoy that. So Madam Richterova, she is in your hands. Examined by Ms. Richterova:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. I would like the usher to show you a piece of paper. Just read the name for yourself and confirm whether yes or not it is your name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This would be Prosecution Exhibit under seal P1689 -- I'm sorry, 1686. Can we go to private session just for some preliminary questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go to private session for a while. Madam when we go to private session, then members of the public won't even -- won't be able to hear what you're saying. The reason is that you'll be Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. giving some details about yourself that would otherwise identify you if others can follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session again, please, for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to show you one document, and it is -- it has already been exhibited. It's P242. I will give you my version. It is a decision dated 12 of June, 1992. It says Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Autonomous Region of Krajina, Crisis Staff Banja Luka, and it is decision to found an agency for population movement and exchange of material wealth for the Autonomous Region of Krajina, and it is signed for president Radoslav Brdjanin. Was this the official title of the agency you started working for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Leave it with the witness so we will need it a little bit later. How did you learn about this company? How did you start working for this company?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: First of all, the agency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Agency, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Do you want me to answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A group of refugees, because refugees were arriving in Banja Luka on a daily basis, so from the group of refugees that had virtually besieged the municipality building at the Crisis Staff, there were people who asked for an organisation to be set up upon their arrival in Banja Luka. So it was upon their request that such an agency was established. Since it was wartime, of course, we did not have adequate means or office equipment. My office happened to have adequate equipment so my husband, together with a lawyer who insisted that such an agency should be set up, offered the equipment that we owned for the use of this agency, and this is how I happened to become an employee of this agency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of the lawyer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Djoko Popovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know where he worked at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I know that he was a lawyer by profession and that he had fled from Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether he had any contacts with municipality, with the municipal assembly or some other authorities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I'm sure he did, because all refugees would gather in front of the town hall every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did he, when you said that the refugees gathered in front of the town hall, did he work for the town hall or what did you know about him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: My husband knew him from before the war, and when I say that refugees gathered in front of the town hall it was because there was no official institution where they could be registered and look for accommodation. At that time, they were still sleeping in school buildings, kindergartens, and that was the reason why they were coming to the municipality building at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And once again, just answer me yes or no, do you know whether this Mr. Popovic worked for the municipality or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I don't know whether he worked for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can see the date on this document as 12 of June.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the agency start working immediately in June or when did it start working?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No, not immediately in June. Sometime in August, but there were Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. preparations going on during that period of time. They were moving offices, the equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the date June, did you know in June about the existence of this agency?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: It did not exist in June yet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when were these discussions about setting up the agency? When did it start?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Sometime in July.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness Exhibit P241.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before it is shown to you do you know the name of a person who was in charge of this agency?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Milos Bojinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is decision issued by Crisis Staff Banja Luka, signed Radoslav Brdjanin, decision to appoint professor Milos -- and it is either Vojinovic or Bojinovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think it's not signed by Mr. Brdjanin, I think it's signed for him. I think it's a "za" document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Richterova, I think he is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read the original document and can you tell us what is the correct name, according to you, from this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Milos Bojinovic [Realtime transcript read in error "Vojinovic"].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, he was appointed on 12th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes, according to this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember when you met Mr. Bojinovic for the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I don't know the exact time but it must have been sometime in late July or early August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me Your Honour there is confusion in the transcript. She was asked what this person's name is and she said it was Milos Vojinovic and the next question is about a person named Bojinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm satisfied it's the same person but the transcript doesn't necessarily reflect that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Unfortunately in this part of the world, or rather from the southern part of Europe, the B and the V is very often mistaken. So it is the same -- I know it's the same person but obviously just for the record we just confirm it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the premises of this agency were located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: In the Mejdan local community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who lived in Mejdan community? What was the ethnicity structure of population in Mejdan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Mixed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there some -- some nationalities which would prevail?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Slightly perhaps. I live in Mejdan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you said slightly, so which ethnicity would be just slightly prevailed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, in brief, the initial activities of this agency? What were your tasks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: The idea was that there should be an agency where Serb refugees could register themselves upon arrival in town. Themselves and members of the families that they had left behind. The records were meant to include also their occupation, their qualifications, what property they had come with, what property they had left behind, and similar information. So that we know who came in town and how many people, how many new people, there were living in town. So that was the idea behind this agency, initially.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said that you registered not only names, places, where they came from, but also qualification, do you know whether the municipality was able to find jobs for these people based on this information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: It was very difficult because at the time nothing was working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But to your knowledge, was it the case or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: Because you also registered the people according to their qualification, so my question was whether it was possible for the municipality to find relevant job for these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No. Because companies were not working. There were no jobs that they could take. And the reason why we recorded their qualifications and professions was because they -- most of them did not bring with them their personal documents, their certificates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you collect any fee for this type of service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how did the agency make its money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: It was the very beginning, we did not need money at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you say it was the beginning. So what happened then, after this initial activities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: The Red Cross, that kept records for non-Serb population, who wanted to leave Banja Luka, brought us these things for us to continue doing them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know when this happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I told you I don't remember the exact dates but it was sometime in August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long approximately again, how long did this first initial activity of registering refugees last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: We continued registering them but until the beginning of the second part of our work, maybe some 15 days, for about 15 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then all of a sudden, you hand -- you were given activities from the Red Cross. Who informed you about the change of your work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Representatives of the Red Cross brought us lists that they had drawn up, and told us that from now on, we would be in charge of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did the non-Serb population learn about the fact that you took over from the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How the non-Serb people learn that it is you, this agency, who will be dealing with registration -- with their registration?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: They were told at the Red Cross that they would no longer be in charge of that but that the agency, that is located in Mejdan, would take over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what -- you said that the Red Cross one day brought you these lists of people and you took -- you took over. What were you are told your new task is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: That we would be in charge of compiling lists, securing transport, going to the separation line with Croatia to take affidavits that people needed when going to Croatia, and similar type of work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the purpose of these lists? What were you doing? What was your task?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Those were the lists that we had to draw up depending on what transport we had available. For example, if we had only one bus, then we would have to draw up a list of people who can be boarded on that bus. If we had two buses then we would make lists accordingly. Those were the lists of non-Serb population which -- who had valid documentations, that was required, for them to be put on the lists, so that they could travel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the purpose of your agency, from this moment, was to prepare a list of non-Serb population who wanted to leave Banja Luka, is it correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes, in addition to the work that we had already started with Serb refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you take us through the registration procedure? How did it start? What one needed if he or she wanted to leave Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: They needed a certificate issued by the local SUP to the effect that they were changing place of residence. They had to have a confirmation letter from a third country, because Croatia did not allow transits if they did not have such letters, because they were afraid that they would remain in Croatia. A certificate issued by the bank to the effect that they had no outstanding debts or loans, and also a receipt certifying that they had paid the required amount of money for the transport.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will start with this changing place of residence. What did it mean? Did it mean that they exchange apartments or they just cancel their residence in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No, not the exchange of apartment. They would just cancel their residence in Banja Luka, because even before the war, whenever someone wanted to change place of residence, he or she was required to come to the SUP and sign a piece of paper stating that he was leaving his place of residence and going some place else so that when he gets to his new place of residence, he can get adequate certificate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they receive a confirmation, they abandon it, their apartment, they cancel the residence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes, the residence. Not that they abandoned their apartments but that they had cancelled their residence with the SUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to that apartment, if they cancelled the residence Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. with the SUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: They would lock them and leave them, but usually they didn't leave at the same time. Usually a member of the family would stay behind when they -- and some left together and would then leave their apartments or houses empty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you mention confirmation letter from a third country. You organised these buses to move non-Serbs out of Banja Luka. Where did you go? Where these people go by these buses? What was their destination?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: To take them to the separation line with Croatia. The place where they were taken was called Dragalic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they taken to some other places or just to Croatia or to the borders with Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Only to the border.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they also taken to some places within Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes, a group went to Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you mentioned this pay slip. So how much these people had to pay for registration to be transferred from Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Not for registration but for the ticket, the travel ticket. I don't exactly remember how much it was, between 30 and 50 German marks but I really cannot remember the exact amount.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you use buses which would belong to this agency, or did you hire private buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No. The agency didn't own buses. They hired buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just stated that the agency took something between 30 and 50 marks, which would be the price of the ticket. How much did you pay to these private companies, these transport companies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I cannot recall the amount.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they receive the -- also the price of the ticket?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I didn't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: She didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question and could you please repeat your answer? The reason is that the interpreters did not hear what you answered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: You stated, "We received from 30 to 50 marks for a ticket." Did you also give the same money to these transport companies? It means one person, let's say 30 deutschmark, because it was the price of a ticket?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No, not the whole sum. It really depended on the price that we agreed upon with the transport company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I'm again returning back to my previous question. How did the agency make its money, if you do not ask for any registration fee and you are asking only for the money which are relevant to the price of one ticket?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: We always tried to negotiate a lower price, and we financed ourselves from the remainder of the money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like to show you a document which we received from the Defence, and our marking is Y001-8261.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document issued Serb Republic of Autonomous Region Krajina-Banja Luka. Your agency -- agency for help in moving of population and exchange of material property. And it is authorisation for these three people and please don't put it on ELMO. To go -- to carry out negotiations with the representatives from the Republic of Croatia regarding the matters concerning moving of population and exchange of material property, and it was signed by Milos Bojinovic. And the date is 10 of August. And you mentioned before that to collect these authorisations or affidavits from Croatia was part of your job, the date for this authorisation was 10 of August. Does it mean that you already started working on this project already at the beginning of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I said I couldn't remember the exact date. It was sometime in August but I really cannot recall the date. Do you want me to explain this document?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I would like you to explain just briefly. Did you go and why did you go to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: We didn't go to Croatia. We went to the separation line, and we went there to fetch the affidavits, the guarantees that were required for those people who were travelling from Banja Luka. The letters that were part of the obligatory bunch of documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If someone wanted to leave Banja Luka but not to Croatia and you mentioned that people were leaving also for Travnik, if someone wanted to leave for Travnik, did he or she need some kind of authorisation as well, some kind of guarantee?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: We started doing Travnik when Croatia prohibited transit over its territory for refugees, and as people of non-Serb ethnicity were constantly pressing us, insisting that they wanted to leave, then we started using Travnik as a route, because no letters of guarantee were required there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated that you took over from the Red Cross. Was there any preparation phase before you started dealing with this particular task?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that these people had to pay or had to bring you this pay slip. Where did they pay this money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: At the post office or at the bank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any special account?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes. The agency had the giro account.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have this account right from the beginning or after you started with this activity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: From the beginning, ever since the agency was registered with the court, under our law, no company or agency may be registered if it doesn't have a giro account in a bank through which payments will be made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one more question about the buses and these companies you used to transfer the non-Serb people from Banja Luka: Do you happen to remember any of these companies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: To begin with, we worked with private entrepreneurs who owned buses. I can't remember their names but there were two men who had a bus each, and because petrol was very expensive they charged a lot. Then we looked for someone whose services would be cheaper, and there was something called, I think it was Autoprevoz Knezevo or something like that, a transport company we discovered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me, one day, these people started coming to your company, they tried to be registered. How many people a day approximately were in front of your agency, were coming to your agency?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Serbs and non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I am asking about non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Many, very many, a great many. The queues were very long. They were there from morning until evening almost, standing there in front of the agency waiting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say many, many people, are we -- and when we are talking about many, many people, are we talking about hundreds? Approximately tell us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it every day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also over weekends or just five working days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Only five working days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you make the final selection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: You mean those who were to leave? Well, people would queue up and those whose turn it was, we didn't make any selection, we just listed people as they came in, provided of course that they had all the required documents and that the documents were in order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you received the required documents, you registered the -- a person. So what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Then we would draw up the list that we had to hand over to the SUP to be checked, we had to inform them. And then we looked for buses and then people travelled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that you had to hand over these lists to the SUP. What was the reason behind this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes. And the reason that the SUP gave was that there were many people who had been indicted or sentenced, people who had stolen something or broken the law, and such people were not allowed to go. They could not evade the law. They had to be held responsible for what they had done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether anyone was taken off the list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Throughout the time I worked in the agency on one occasion, one man was taken off the list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you learn why he was taken off the list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes. He was one of seven people who had been members of the SDA and founded a young Muslim organisation. They called the Muslim people to arm themselves and to rebel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many convoys did you organise per week or per month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Throughout the time I worked there, perhaps six.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you organise --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Or maybe seven times we did this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you organise convoys, or did you manage to organise convoys, every week?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how often?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Maybe once or twice a month. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, -- and again, how many buses form such a convoy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Well, it varied, depending on how many we could get. Sometimes there was one, sometimes three.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you say not every week, so approximately how often you managed to organise these convoys?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Once or twice a month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, I will ask for how long did you organise these convoys, or better say, for how long did you work for this agency and organise the convoys?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I worked in the agency until the end of December, 1992. The organisation of the convoys did not depend on us but also on the other side. Sometimes we would secure transport, prepare people, and then one of the negotiators would go to Dragalic to say a convoy was to arrive on the next day and Croatia refused to accept the people. Then we would have to postpone the convoy and wait until Croatia was ready to receive them. Sometimes we would wait 15 days, a month, two, it all depended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will show you one more document -- or I will show you two documents. If this Exhibit P288 and the other one is payroll, it's a Defence document, with our markings Y001-8263. This document P288, it's from the radio, unfortunately we do not have the interview itself, but it says that our reporter, Dragan Stegic talked about the passport in the agency with its president, Milos Bojinovic. And the date of this interview was 23rd of July, 1992. I know that you said that you do not remember now when exactly you started working for this agency, but if you look at this document dated 23rd of July, and Milos Bojinovic was supposed to talk about the work of the agency, to your knowledge, is it possible that the agency worked already in July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No, no. It didn't work in July. In July we were carrying out preparations but would you please give me sometime to read this? I haven't read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please. This document doesn't say anything about the content of the interview. It just says that the interview was conducted with Milos Bojinovic and the date. The other document is payroll from July. So did you work already for the agency in July? You stated that there was some preparation phase. Was it possible that it was in July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: That was when we were carrying out preparations, and as for this payroll, it could have been drawn up retroactively in order for us to be paid for the work we did at the time, because in the first few months, we didn't have any money. I said that the agency financed itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The amount of money was around 20.000 dinars. Is it correct you were paid in dinars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes. Our currency at that time was the dinar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if the witness could be shown document Y001-8259, which is a payroll from December? And can you see your name on this payroll?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the money paid are around 70.000 dinars, so the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- Agency was earning money to pay you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that the agency was earning money just from the payment of the tickets for the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes, and the taxes they paid at the time, we started carrying out exchanges of flats, and people both Serbs and non-Serbs would pay a tax of I think five marks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did your agency start dealing with this activity? I mean the exchange of apartments. When did you start?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I told you I have a very poor memory for dates but it could have been in August or September. I really couldn't pinpoint the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You worked, as we heard, approximately for four or five months, July you mentioned the preparation phase, August we have this authorisation, so you already started dealing with Croatian part. September, October, November, December. So within these five months, was it right from the beginning? Was it in the middle? Or was it at the end of the time, you worked for this company, for this agency?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: You mean the exchange of apartments?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The exchange of apartments.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Well, let's say sometime in the middle of the time I worked there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who came with this idea?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: To me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Madam, while we are in open session, try to avoid either mentioning names or giving details which could identify you. We are trying to protect you. At the same time you're trying to reveal your identity without obviously realising that so we are taking care of that. We are going to redact that from the public transcript or transcript which would be available to the public. Yes, Madam Richterova, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was more or less your idea based on your experience with other people who managed to exchange such apartment, is it correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how was the agency involved in this exchange of apartments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Legal advice we had form -- or rather there was a form that could be bought in shops, in book shops, for the buying and selling of real estate and people would come and fill this in and bring it to us and then we would give them advice and then the contracts would be validated by the authorities on both sides, because for a contract to be valid, it would have to have the seal of both governments on both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you provided the legal advice. Did you ask Mr. Bojinovic whether it is possible to provide this type of service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he agreed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how much did you charge for this type of service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: As I said, I think five marks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you receive this money in cash or again was it put on the account?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No, no, not in cash. It was all through the account.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, approximately how many people utilised this service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I think quite a few, but when I left all the documentation stayed there. So I couldn't tell you now but I think that these contracts on the exchange of property, they all remained in the agency when I left it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you able to tell us at least approximately whether it was more than ten, more than 100, more than 200?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: More, more than 100. Much more than a hundred, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you say much more than 100, was it more than 1.000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before we will have a break can we go to a private session for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go to private session for a while please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I said that the agency was not opened to carry out the moving out of non-Serbs, but to help the Serbs coming into Banja Luka every day who had no where to register and no one to look after them. They slept in schools, kindergartens, sports halls, even in the streets, and then it happened that the Red Cross transferred the lists but we didn't distinguish between ethnicity -- ethnicities. We didn't draw any distinctions. We helped every one who wanted to leave. I think mostly they wanted to leave because they were afraid of the large number of Serbs coming in. Banja Luka was the only place where there was no war going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We will discuss this after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We will have a break until 11.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes, Mr. Brdjanin is back. So Madam Richterova, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Sorry about that. Madam Richterova, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, were you ever present when people were leaving Banja Luka and it was still organised by the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times were you present, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Several times, when my school friends and colleagues were leaving, those who were of non-Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again approximately how many buses did you see leaving during the occasions when you were present there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I'm not able to tell you the exact number but on those several occasions when I went, there would be two buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So each time, just to clarify it, each time you were there, there was approximately two buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know how often Red Cross organised these convoys?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said several times you were present several times. What was -- what were the gaps between these departures?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, maybe every 10 or 20 days. I mean, I was -- I wasn't present when buses were leaving at all times. Only when I went there to greet my friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you know what buses the Red Cross was using? Were they private -- excuse me, were they buses from private companies or from municipality or do you know it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you took over from the Red Cross, compiling these lists, did you took over also buses or the companies which were -- which were providing this service for the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Two privately owned buses were offered to us by their owners. They told us they had previously worked for the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my question was: Did Red Cross maybe gave you a list of companies which they were using for transport?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, to clarify how many people left Banja Luka via your agency, you stated you worked for this agency approximately from August until December, which is five months, and you stated that the agency organised probably only six convoys while you were working there, is it correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Approximately six. Again, I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you stated that you -- when you organised only these approximately six convoys, that you had two or three buses, which would mean that you transferred or you provided your service only to approximately 300 -- from 300 to 400 people, is it correct, or were there more people who left Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Well, there are often 40 seats on a bus, so there is -- it's 18 times 4, something over 100 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The interpreters -- the last words that we heard was something over 100, but we get the impression that the interpretation was interrupted. Madam, could I ask to you repeat your answer? They said -- you said, well, there are often 40 seats on a bus, so there is -- it's 18 times 4, something over a hundred. Did you say anything else beyond that or was that the end of your testimony, of your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Something over a hundred, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you want to say that in one convoy, there were approximately 100 people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps at this point, madam, before I decide to intervene in a much stronger manner, the witness could tell us how much she reckons her agency or the agency she worked for, how many people they -- she -- that that agency moved out of the area it was responsible for, how many that Caritas and how many did Merhamet, because she mentioned both, and how many did the Red Cross, because the numbers must tally. Otherwise, someone is not telling us the truth and if I catch anyone not telling us the truth, there will be fire works in this room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, within these five months, you were compiling these lists, you were giving these lists to police for clearance. Approximately within these five months, how many people left Banja Luka via your agency? Was it more than 100? Was it more than 500? Was it more than 1.000? Was it less?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Via our agency, the number would be 1.000, between 600 and 1.000, during the time when I worked there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your agency was financed just from the incomes you received from these people who were buying tickets to leave Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes, and the people who had paid the tax for the exchange of their apartments and houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps she could work out a little bit of arithmetic here, a little bit of mathematics because at the rate that she mentioned earlier, that these persons were paying, which would be -- she should put us in a position whereby we can see whether the figures at least that are shown on the pay slips or the pay statements for December in particular, whether they tally or not. Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the problem is we don't know how marks and dinars relate in December of 1992 because the pay slips show dinars and the people were paying marks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, in marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think 20.000 dinars was I think less than 100 marks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. That's why I'm asking the witness to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you heard the question which was asked by the Judge. Was it -- was the income from these tickets and the fee for legal advice sufficient to provide salary for 11 people working in the agency?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes, but that income -- or rather those salaries were not very high.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you by any chance remember what was the exchange rate between dinar and deutschmark at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No. I -- not exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did anyone bother to pay you in dinars at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So she didn't have to bother about the exchange rate, Madam Richterova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, last question regarding this subject: Do you know approximately how many people left with Caritas and Merhamet? Did you cooperate with these humanitarian organisations? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No, no. We didn't cooperate with them, and I don't know how many people left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I said before, I will change the subject. At the beginning, I showed you the document, decision to found an agency for population movement, and it was stamped by Radoslav Brdjanin or I'm sorry, it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was stamped for Radoslav Brdjanin. Did you know Radoslav Brdjanin in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Only from the media. He was one of the people who were in power at the time and we all knew him, but I personally didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you know what was his position at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No, not exactly. I know that he was one of the leaders but I don't know what kind of position he held.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I show you this document that it was issued by Crisis Staff. Did you know whether or not Mr. Brdjanin was a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't learn via media what was his position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: At the time, there were often power shortages, and we couldn't follow the media all the time. I know that he was a member of the top leadership, that he was in local government but I was not aware of the function he performed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him talking on television, on -- did you hear him on radio or did you see any rallies in which he would participate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object unless there is a time frame set, if she is going to talk about 1995 or 75.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct. Please put a time frame to your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about year 1991 and 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No. Not in 1992, because Banja Luka was in total dark practically speaking and very rarely could one listen to the media, but people sometimes tried to improvise broadcasting. I had heard Radoslav Brdjanin speaking on rallies at the time when these divisions between a local authorities occurred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was it? Again approximately. Which year, which period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I think it was in 1991. I don't know exactly when the political parties were established along ethnic lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said approximately in 1991?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was it in the beginning, towards the end of 1991? Because 1991 is like any other year, it's 12 months, and 12 months is quite a long time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know exactly when the national parties won in Bosnia and Herzegovina but I know that both SDA and SDS held daily rallies at the square [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you remember hearing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Hearing from?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I personally didn't attend those pre-electoral rallies so I didn't hear anything directly from Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the answer at page 39, line 21, also included HDZ, which didn't make it into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Do you agree to that, Madam? Did you also mention HDZ apart from SDA and SDS, having daily rallies at the square?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't attend these rallies. What did you hear from others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: At that time, all three parties, both gave and requested support from their people, SDS, SDA and HDZ. They talked more or less in the same context, all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you watch TV in 1991? Did you see any political leaders --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- On television in 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see Mr. Brdjanin on television in 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Brdjanin was a representative of the Serb people, so of course he was on TV.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that it is 10, 11 years ago, but do you remember anything what was said by Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember hearing any other representatives of the SDS speaking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No. I mean I did hear something but I don't think I'm able to repeat any of those words.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember hearing any representatives of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: The same, the answer is the same. I did hear, but I couldn't repeat what they said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about in 1992? Were you able to watch television in the first half of the year 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Maybe sometime at the beginning of that year, up until the month of March, but we didn't have electricity every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't have electricity from the beginning of the year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes, approximately from that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the time when you had electricity, were you able to see any politicians on TV or listen to them on the radio?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I didn't have time to watch politicians. It was more important for me to switch on the washing machine and take care of the laundry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you cannot tell us what was your impression about Mr. Brdjanin? Was he popular in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Just what I know from the people who came to the agency, the Serbs who visited the agency. Apparently Mr. Brdjanin was very well liked amongst the people, because according to their stories, he was the only man who wanted and endeavoured to help them ease their troubles. This is at least what the Serbs who came to the agency told us. They praised him a lot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he was popular with the Serb population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear any comments on Mr. Brdjanin from the non-Serb population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Back to the agency. To your knowledge, what was the reason for non-Serbs leaving Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I think that the main reason for non-Serbs leaving Banja Luka was the fear from the influx of the Serb population in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you describe the atmosphere in Banja Luka from, let's say, March until the end of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: How shall I describe it to you? It was terrible. There were a lot of refugees around. The whole town was in chaos. The electricity was often cut off. We didn't have enough food, enough medicine, enough water. People kept coming in on a daily basis, people came in, other people left, it was total chaos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say people were coming, which nationality are you referring to, to be more specific?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: To Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the people who were leaving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said it was chaotic, no electricity. What about jobs? Could people work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: 90 per cent of the companies were not working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether there were some dismissals from work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: There were some, but on the other hand, there was no need to dismiss anyone, because, as I said, 90 per cent of the companies were not working at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If someone was dismissed, to your knowledge, what was the reason for dismissal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Well, I think it was because many people went to the front line, because they were mobilised, there was no water or electricity, as a result of that, many companies were not operational, so that was the main reason, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What mobilisation had to do with dismissals or better say with my question what was the reason for dismissals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: At the beginning of the war, all three ethnic groups received call-up notes, not only Serbs, but members of all three groups, and of course, if someone responded to the call-up, they couldn't work, but what happened was that if all the Serbs went to the front line, responding to the call-up, then you couldn't have only the non-Serbs working, and the Serbs fighting the non-Serbs, on the confrontation lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, are you aware of any non-Serb directors of firms which would be dismissed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No, but I can tell you that my sister's husband, who was not a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Serb, responded to the call-up, and he remained the managing director of his company until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were there any checkpoints in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: There were no checkpoints in Banja Luka. There were only checkpoints at the points of entry and exit from the town, but there were no checkpoints within the town itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was any checkpoint in your neighbourhood, in Mejdan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were there any searches, searches of houses or searches on people, in the period of March until December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When people were leaving Banja Luka, were they allowed to take everything with them or were there some limits what they are allowed to take with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: There were no limits. They could even organise transport of their furniture to other areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about money? Were they allowed to take unlimited amount of money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No. I never had any document limiting the amount of money. I know we were told they couldn't take weapons or military booklets. That's what they couldn't take. Also, cameras and video cameras.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness a document. I showed you this document yesterday. It's P227, and you can use my copy, because it's one page from Official Gazettes. And it was a decision issued on 3rd June, 1992 and under Article 3, it says, "Natural persons leaving the Autonomous Region of Krajina may take out a maximum of 300 deutschmarks or corresponding amount in other currencies which may not exceed this limit."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I have never seen this document before. This document was never delivered to us in the agency, nor did anyone tell us that that's how things should be. People may have known this, they may have read this, but nobody ever asked us how much money they were allowed to take, nor did we have this information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they -- when people were boarding the buses, were they searched?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes. They were searched. Their belongings were searched so that we would see they were not taking things that were prohibited, that is weapons, their military identity booklet, a camera or a video camera or a video cassette.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, were these people searched during the transport, either to Croatia or to Travnik? Were they searched on the way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No, no. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never received any information from people who left and returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these buses escorted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes. The police did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And back to the situation in Banja Luka in 1992, are you aware of the group of people called red Kombi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have never heard about this group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about them but I never saw that van.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you heard about them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Just that there was this van, they were calling the red van, which was allegedly driving non-Serbs out of Banja Luka. I never saw this, and I never heard from any of my non-Serb friends that they had had any contacts with the red Kombi or the red van.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you heard that they would be abusing someone on the street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you heard about a group called SOS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: When I had my first interview, I really didn't know what this SOS meant. Then later it was explained for me that it stood for Serbian defence forces, and that this was the regular army, because of course the JNA had ceased to exist so that the Serb army of the Krajina was called that. They were the Serbian defence forces. Because the JNA was no longer there. So that's what the army was called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Madam Richterova, because you moved on from the red Kombi to something else, and I want to have this clarified, probably the -- you were asked very directly whether you had ever heard any allegations of abuses of citizens in Banja Luka by or related to the existence of this red Kombi or the people who used to be in this red Kombi. Did you ever hear anyone talk about this red Kombi being used by whoever used to run it, abuse citizens in Banja Luka? Or was it just another charitable institution carrying out a charitable work of helping people out of Banja Luka and to somewhere else? What, according to you, from what you heard at the time, what did this red Kombi stand for? Charitable service? Or abuse of citizens?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I've just said I never saw this van. I don't know if it was really red. Someone would have recognised it. I heard of its existence but I never saw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will read to you a transcript of the questions that were put to you and your answers during your interview with Mr. Dupas and Madam Korner. Mr. Dupas told you, "We have spoken to several witnesses who described this notorious red Kombi that was driving -- driven around Banja Luka in the year 1992 and harassing the non-Serb population. Do you have any information about that?" And you answered: "I also heard that. I also knew about that from stories." And then Mr. Dupas told you, "What were the stories that were going around?" And you said, "All the citizens of Banja Luka knew that, that there was this Kombi that was abusing people in the city." When you say people, he said, Mr. Dupas, you're talking about non-Serbs? And you said, "Also the Serbs who wanted to protect the non-Serbs."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as I said, just now, I only heard people talking about this Kombi but I never saw it myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you heard people talk about this red Kombi positively or negatively?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's "da."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Negatively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we got it at last. It's like being in a dentist's clinic now, having to extract one tooth after the other. Yes, Madam Richterova?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the role of the SOS in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I've just told you I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said -- you said that people -- there were Serbs coming to Banja Luka, there were convoys of Serbs coming to Banja Luka. Where were they accommodated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: In the Borik sports hall, the Mejdan sports hall, the Mejdan kindergarten and the primary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there any period of time when these people move into the houses which were abandoned by people, by non-Serb people who left Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when was it approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I have no idea when. Throughout this time, people searched for empty houses and when they found one, they entered it and settled down in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, I will return to the politicians in Banja Luka, and I would like to ask you if you remember, during the 1991, stating anything negative from the Serb politicians towards non-Serb population in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: I was never active in politics. I was never interested in politics. I never attended the rallies. I didn't hear what any of them said, because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were able to watch television, or at least read newspapers. Neither from these medias you learned anything which we could call negative attitude towards non-Serb population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: At all these rallies all the leaders depending on the part they represented talked within their own context. Some people said let's start from the Serbs, that the Serbs had to organise themselves, to protect themselves that the Muslims were arming. And then the next day the SDA would turn up on the Krajina square and the SDA leaders would then say that they had knowledge that the Serbs were armed, that they had to organise themselves, that they had to protect themselves. On the third day, the HDZ would turn up and say the same things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will leave this unless Your Honour will read the witness her testimony given in Banja Luka on the page 36.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. The witness is in your hands, Ms. -- Madam Richterova. We won't intervene unless it is really something --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall stating to the questions, can you remember exact words what was his attitude and this question was referring to Mr. Brdjanin, as expressed in his speeches towards the non-Serbs in Banja Luka? Do you recall this question and the answer to this question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Yes, I remember being asked this question and I think I replied that -- oh, I don't know exactly what I replied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You replied, "Well, how could I tell you that? Of course it wasn't positive but you know how could I tell you this when I had no contact with this person? I never met him personally." Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. You said it wasn't positive. Now you say that you have never heard anything. Can you explain to us this inconsistent reply?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT88
utterances.text: Well, I think it's not inconsistent. When I said negative, it's what I just explained. All three ethnic parties said the same sort of thing, and of course the things Mr. Brdjanin said at pre-electoral rallies was negative for the non-Serbs. By the same token the other parties that spoke at pre-electoral rallies on behalf of the SDA and the HDZ, what they said was negative for the Serbian people. That's what I meant when I said negative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps she could also tell us what the position was, whether it changed in the post electoral -- and that's after the formation of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. We probably are more interested to hear about what happened during that phase rather than in the post election or pre-election phase of the events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will repeat the question: You discuss this phase, 1991, when there were these rallies of all three parties, but what was the situation after the election and after the takeover?
